subproblem.title: Liouville theorem: C^{1,alpha} entire weak solutions of constant-coefficient Legendre systems have constant gradient
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, 0 < alpha < 1, lam > 0, Lam and K real. Let A be a continuous bilinear form on L := L(R^n, R^l) with A[P][P] >= lam ||P||^2 and |A[P][Q]| <= Lam ||P|| ||Q|| for all P, Q. Let W : R^n -> R^l be C^1 with ||DW(x) - DW(y)|| <= K |x - y|^alpha for all x, y. Assume the integral over R^n of A[DW(x)][Dzeta(x)] is 0 for every C^1 compactly supported zeta : R^n -> R^l. Then DW(x) = DW(y) for all x, y in R^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (α lam Lam K : ℝ) (A : (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (W : Rn n → Rn ℓ), 0 < α → α < 1 → 0 < lam → (∀ P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, lam * ‖P‖ ^ 2 ≤ A P P) → (∀ P Q : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, |A P Q| ≤ Lam * ‖P‖ * ‖Q‖) → ContDiff ℝ 1 W → (∀ x y : Rn n, ‖fderiv ℝ W x - fderiv ℝ W y‖ ≤ K * ‖x - y‖ ^ α) → (∀ ζ : Rn n → Rn ℓ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → ∫ x, A (fderiv ℝ W x) (fderiv ℝ ζ x) = 0) → ∀ x y : Rn n, fderiv ℝ W x = fderiv ℝ W y
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (Liouville theorem), with the details filled in.
Notation. L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm; e_1, ..., e_n is the standard basis of R^n. A C^1 map V : R^n -> R^l is called a global solution if the integral over R^n of A[DV(x)][Dzeta(x)] is 0 for every C^1 compactly supported zeta : R^n -> R^l. For C^1 maps V this integrand is continuous and vanishes outside tsupport zeta, so it is integrable. For s in {1..n}, write d_s V := DV(.) e_s, and d_{s_1} d_{s_2} ... d_{s_k} V := d_{s_1}(d_{s_2}( ... d_{s_k} V)). Lower integrals ∫⁻ take values in [0, infinity] (Lean: ∫⁻ with ‖.‖ₑ ^ 2).
0. Reductions. If n = 0, R^0 is a single point and there is nothing to prove; assume n >= 1. Replace Lam by Lam+ := max(Lam, 0) and K by K+ := max(K, 0); the hypotheses still hold. Let C3 >= 0 be the constant of the sibling caccioppoli lemma for (n, l, lam, Lam+).
1. Mollification (parent 4a). Fix phi in C_c^infinity(R^n) with phi >= 0, support in B_1(0), and integral 1 (for example the normalized ContDiffBump with radii 1/2 < 1; ContDiffBump.integral_normed). For eps > 0 put phi_eps(z) := eps^{-n} phi(z/eps). It is C^infinity, nonnegative, supported in B_eps(0), and has integral 1. Put W_eps(x) := integral of phi_eps(z) W(x - z) dz.
 (a) W_eps is C^infinity. It is the convolution of the C_c^infinity function phi_eps with the continuous, hence locally integrable, function W (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
 (b) DW_eps(x) = integral of phi_eps(z) DW(x - z) dz for every x. This is differentiation under the integral sign (hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_of_fderiv_le). For x' in B_1(x), the x'-derivative of phi_eps(z) W(x' - z) is phi_eps(z) DW(x' - z). It is bounded by (sup phi_eps) (sup of ||DW|| over closedBall(x, 1 + eps)) 1_{B_eps(0)}(z), which is integrable in z; and DW is continuous.
 (c) For all x, x': ||DW_eps(x) - DW_eps(x')|| <= integral of phi_eps(z) ||DW(x - z) - DW(x' - z)|| dz <= K+ |x - x'|^alpha.
 (d) ||DW_eps(x) - DW(x)|| <= integral of phi_eps(z) ||DW(x - z) - DW(x)|| dz <= K+ eps^alpha, which tends to 0 as eps -> 0.
 (e) W_eps is a global solution. Let zeta be C^1 with compact support. The map P -> A[P][Dzeta(x)] is a continuous linear form on L, so by (b), A[DW_eps(x)][Dzeta(x)] = integral of phi_eps(z) A[DW(x - z)][Dzeta(x)] dz. The function (x, z) -> phi_eps(z) A[DW(x - z)][Dzeta(x)] is continuous on R^n x R^n and supported in the compact set tsupport zeta x closedBall(0, eps), so it is integrable. By Fubini, the integral of A[DW_eps][Dzeta] dx equals the integral over z of phi_eps(z) times (integral of A[DW(x - z)][Dzeta(x)] dx). For fixed z, substitute x = x' + z. The inner integral becomes the integral of A[DW(x')][Dzeta_z(x')] dx', where zeta_z := zeta(. + z) is C^1 with compact support and Dzeta_z(x') = Dzeta(x' + z). This inner integral is 0. Hence the integral of A[DW_eps][Dzeta] is 0.
2. Partial derivatives of smooth global solutions (parent 4b). Claim: if V is C^infinity and a global solution and s is in {1..n}, then d_s V is C^infinity and a global solution. d_s V is C^infinity, being the composition of DV with evaluation at e_s. Fix a C^1 compactly supported zeta and let T := tsupport zeta, a compact set.
 (i) For h != 0 put V_h(x) := (V(x + h e_s) - V(x))/h, so DV_h(x) = (DV(x + h e_s) - DV(x))/h. By translation invariance of Lebesgue measure, the integral of A[DV(x + h e_s)][Dzeta(x)] dx equals the integral of A[DV(x')][Dzeta(x' - h e_s)] dx'. This is 0, because zeta(. - h e_s) is C^1 with compact support and its derivative at x' is Dzeta(x' - h e_s). Together with the integral of A[DV][Dzeta] being 0, linearity gives that the integral of A[DV_h][Dzeta] is 0 (all integrands are continuous with compact support).
 (ii) Let D^2V(x) be the derivative at x of x -> DV(x), and D^2V(x)(u) in L its value at u. Apply the mean value inequality to tau -> DV(x + tau e_s) - tau D^2V(x)(e_s) between 0 and h. It gives ||DV_h(x) - D^2V(x)(e_s)|| <= sup over |tau| <= |h| of ||D^2V(x + tau e_s) - D^2V(x)||. As h -> 0 this tends to 0 uniformly for x in T, because D^2V is uniformly continuous on the compact set T + closedBall(0, 1).
 (iii) For all x and h' in R^n, D(d_s V)(x)h' = D^2V(x)(h')(e_s) = D^2V(x)(e_s)(h'). The second equality is the symmetry of the second derivative of a C^2 map (ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt). Hence DV_h -> D(d_s V) uniformly on T.
 (iv) |integral of A[DV_h][Dzeta] - integral of A[D(d_s V)][Dzeta]| <= Lam+ (sup over T of ||DV_h - D(d_s V)||) (integral of ||Dzeta||), which tends to 0. Hence the integral of A[D(d_s V)][Dzeta] is the limit of 0 as h -> 0, i.e. 0.
 By (1e) and induction on k: for every eps > 0, k >= 0 and (s_1, ..., s_k) in {1..n}^k, the map d_{s_1} ... d_{s_k} W_eps is C^infinity and a global solution.
3. Iterated Caccioppoli (parent 4c). Fix eps > 0. For k >= 1 and rho > 0 let Q_k(rho) be the sum over (s_1..s_k) in {1..n}^k of the lower integral over B_rho(0) of ||D(d_{s_1} ... d_{s_k} W_eps)||_e^2. It is finite, since the integrands are continuous and B_rho(0) is bounded. Claim: for every P in L, rho > 0 and k >= 1, Q_k(rho) <= (n C3)^k rho^{-2k} times the lower integral over B_{2^k rho}(0) of ||DW_eps - P||_e^2.
 Case k = 1. Fix s. V := d_s W_eps is C^1 and a global solution. In particular the integral of A[DV][Dzeta] is 0 for every C^1 compactly supported zeta with tsupport zeta in B_{2 rho}(0). The caccioppoli lemma with y = 0 and c = P e_s gives: lower integral over B_rho of ||DV||_e^2 <= (C3/rho^2) times the lower integral over B_{2 rho} of |DW_eps(x)e_s - P e_s|_e^2, which is <= (C3/rho^2) times the lower integral over B_{2 rho} of ||DW_eps - P||_e^2, because |T e_s| <= ||T||. Sum over the n values of s.
 Case k -> k + 1. Fix (s_0, s_1, ..., s_k) and put U := d_{s_1} ... d_{s_k} W_eps and V := d_{s_0} U = DU(.) e_{s_0}. V is C^1 and a global solution. The caccioppoli lemma with c = 0 gives: lower integral over B_rho of ||DV||_e^2 <= (C3/rho^2) (lower integral over B_{2 rho} of |V|_e^2) <= (C3/rho^2) (lower integral over B_{2 rho} of ||DU||_e^2). Sum over s_0 (n values) and over (s_1..s_k): Q_{k+1}(rho) <= n C3 rho^{-2} Q_k(2 rho). By the induction hypothesis this is <= n C3 rho^{-2} (n C3)^k (2 rho)^{-2k} times the lower integral over B_{2^{k+1} rho} of ||DW_eps - P||_e^2, which is <= (n C3)^{k+1} rho^{-2(k+1)} times the same integral.
4. Vanishing of all partial derivatives of order n + 2 (parent 4d). Take P := DW_eps(0) and k := n + 1. By (1c), ||DW_eps(x) - P|| <= K+ |x|^alpha <= K+ (2^k rho)^alpha for x in B_{2^k rho}(0). Since vol(B_r(0)) = r^n vol(B_1(0)) < infinity, the lower integral over B_{2^k rho} of ||DW_eps - P||_e^2 is <= vol(B_1) (2^k rho)^n K+^2 (2^k rho)^{2 alpha}. Hence Q_{n+1}(rho) <= c' rho^{2 alpha - n - 2}, with c' := (n C3)^{n+1} vol(B_1) K+^2 2^{(n+1)(n + 2 alpha)} independent of rho. Since 2 alpha - n - 2 < 0, this bound tends to 0 as rho -> infinity. Q_{n+1} is nondecreasing in rho, because B_rho is contained in B_rho' for rho <= rho'. So Q_{n+1}(rho) <= Q_{n+1}(rho') <= c' rho'^{2 alpha - n - 2} for all rho' >= rho, and therefore Q_{n+1}(rho) = 0 for every rho > 0. Each summand then vanishes: the lower integral over B_rho of ||D(d_{s_1} ... d_{s_{n+1}} W_eps)||_e^2 is 0. The integrand is continuous and every nonempty open subset of B_rho(0) has positive measure, so D(d_{s_1} ... d_{s_{n+1}} W_eps) = 0 on B_rho(0) for every rho, i.e. on R^n. Since D(d_{s_1} ... d_{s_{n+1}} W_eps)(x) e_{s_0} = d_{s_0} d_{s_1} ... d_{s_{n+1}} W_eps(x), all iterated partial derivatives d_{s_0} d_{s_1} ... d_{s_{n+1}} W_eps of order n + 2 vanish identically, for every index tuple.
5. DW_eps is constant (parent 4e). Fix x in R^n and let p(t) := DW_eps(t x) - DW_eps(0), an element of L, for t in R. For r in {1..n} let g_r := d_r W_eps = DW_eps(.) e_r, a C^infinity map. By induction on j, the j-th derivative of t -> g_r(t x) is the sum over (s_1..s_j) of x_{s_1} ... x_{s_j} (d_{s_1} ... d_{s_j} g_r)(t x). Indeed, the derivative of t -> f(t x) is sum_s x_s (d_s f)(t x). For j = n + 1, each term d_{s_1} ... d_{s_{n+1}} g_r = d_{s_1} ... d_{s_{n+1}} d_r W_eps is an iterated partial derivative of order n + 2 of W_eps, which vanishes by step 4. Hence t -> g_r(t x) is C^infinity with identically vanishing (n+1)-st derivative. So it is a polynomial in t of degree <= n (Taylor's formula with zero remainder, applied to each real coordinate). Since an element of L is determined by its values on e_1..e_n, p(t) = sum_{i=0}^{n} c_i t^i with c_i in L, and c_0 = p(0) = 0. By (1c), ||p(t)|| <= K+ |t x|^alpha = K+ |x|^alpha |t|^alpha. Suppose some c_i != 0, and let i0 >= 1 be the largest such index. For t >= 1, ||p(t)|| >= ||c_{i0}|| t^{i0} - sum_{i < i0} ||c_i|| t^i. So ||p(t)|| / t^{i0} -> ||c_{i0}|| > 0 as t -> infinity. On the other hand ||p(t)|| / t^{i0} <= K+ |x|^alpha t^{alpha - i0} -> 0, because i0 >= 1 > alpha. This is a contradiction. Hence p = 0, i.e. DW_eps(x) = DW_eps(0) for every x.
6. Conclusion (parent 4f). For x, x' in R^n and eps > 0, (1d) and step 5 give ||DW(x) - DW(x')|| <= ||DW(x) - DW_eps(x)|| + ||DW_eps(x) - DW_eps(x')|| + ||DW_eps(x') - DW(x')|| <= 2 K+ eps^alpha. Letting eps -> 0 gives DW(x) = DW(x'). QED

proof_key_steps: reduce to n >= 1 and Lam, K >= 0; take C3 from the caccioppoli lemma
mollify: W_eps is smooth, DW_eps = phi_eps * DW keeps the Hoelder bound, DW_eps -> DW pointwise, and W_eps is a global solution (Fubini + translated test functions)
difference quotients and symmetry of D^2: partial derivatives of smooth global solutions are global solutions
iterated Caccioppoli: Q_k(rho) <= (n C3)^k rho^{-2k} times the integral over B_{2^k rho} of ||DW_eps - P||^2
with P = DW_eps(0) and k = n+1: Q_{n+1}(rho) <= c' rho^{2alpha - n - 2} -> 0; Q_{n+1} is monotone, so every partial derivative of order n+2 vanishes
t -> DW_eps(tx) - DW_eps(0) is a polynomial of degree <= n with growth <= K|x|^alpha |t|^alpha, hence 0

audit.reason: The exact global weak-solution statement is proved using only the declared Caccioppoli dependency and library facts. Mollification and difference quotients preserve the equation; iterated Caccioppoli yields the negative exponent 2 alpha - n - 2. Consequently high derivatives vanish, and sublinear gradient growth forces the resulting polynomial to be constant. The final mollification limit and the n = 0 case are justified.
